name: NIST SP 800-218A
full_name: NIST SP 800-218A Secure Software Development Practices for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models: SSDF Community Profile
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
notice: SP 800-218A is an SSDF Community Profile for AI model development. Each SSDF task carries NIST's AI-specific priority; its recommendations are the test points, and NIST's considerations, notes and informative references are shown as guidance. All text is quoted from the publication.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-218A, Secure Software Development Practices for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models

control_flags.type: task: an SSDF task as profiled for AI model development.
control_flags.priority: NIST's AI model development priority for the task: High, Medium or Low.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable tasks performed, with partial performance counting as half. NIST defines no score; this is an HCG measure.

rules.summary: A task is performed only when each of its applicable recommendations is followed.
The profile applies to producers of AI models, producers of AI systems that use those models, and acquirers of those systems; tasks outside the organization's role are marked not applicable.
rules.quote: This document is that companion resource.

rules.summary: A partially performed task counts as half. This is an HCG convention.

glossary.definition: Secure Software Development Framework, NIST SP 800-218: practices for producing secure software.

An AI model trained on broad data, generally using self-supervision, with at least tens of billions of parameters, applicable across a wide range of contexts, that exhibits or could be modified to exhibit high performance at tasks posing serious security risks.
The numerical parameters learned during training that determine a model's outputs.
